description:
FILED AND FIXED s469bh (Opus, 2026-09-05) while widening the subscript use
classification for #1056.  PRE-EXISTING on main `c80b1a0` -- reproduced there
in a worktree, with byte-identical emission, so the widening did not create it.

== THE BUG ==

`box-set` on a NON-box returns the value and stores nothing.  That is
deliberate (`undef = val` is a perl no-op and *p-undef* is not a box), and it
is the DEFAULT arm of all four incdec macros -- the arm a bare `$x` reaches:

    (t `(box-set ,real-place (perl-decrement ,real-place)))

A slot with a raw verdict (raw-slot / the B-regime freeze,
docs/raw-numeric-verdict.md) holds the VALUE, not a box.  So `--$i` on such a
slot computed the new value and threw it away.

Parser2 HAS a raw twin -- p-incf-raw / p-decf-raw -- but it fires only when
the incdec IS the whole statement (`_lower_expr_statement`, the `!$mod &&
@$expr == 2` arm).  A value-CONSUMING incdec falls through the expression
generator, which has no access to the verdicts at all
(`grep -n unboxable Pl/ExprToCL.pm` is empty), and emits the boxed macro.
That disagreement between the verdict and the emission is the bug.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; loops forever under ./runpcl on c80b1a0):

    my @a = (10, 20, 30, 40, 50);
    my $t = 0;
    for (my $i = @a; -- $i;) { $t += $a[$i]; }
    print "$t\n";                 # perl: 140     PCL c80b1a0: hangs

`$i`'s uses are all `num` (an array subscript), its write shape is unproven
(an array in scalar context), so the B regime freezes it raw -- and then the
condition never moves.

WHERE THE HOLE IS, exactly: an incdec in a C-style for CONDITION, either
fixity.  Everywhere else VarAnnotator records `write-incdec` for a
value-consuming incdec and the slot stays boxed (measured with PCL_B_DEBUG
over eleven shapes: `my $v = $x++`, `while (--$c)`, `$t += $a[$k-1] while
--$k`, the magical string increment, undef, a numeric string -- all boxed).
The C-for condition is the one position that does not record the event.

== THE FIX (shipped s469bh) ==

ONE store-back decision shared by the four macros, rule 11 -- not four
emitter branches, and not a VarAnnotator event (which would have BOXED the
slot and lost the optimization instead of making the two agree):

    (eval-when (:compile-toplevel :load-toplevel :execute)
      (defun %p-incdec-store-form (place new-form)
        (if (symbolp place)
            `(if (p-box-p ,place) (box-set ,place ,new-form) (setf ,place ,new-form))
            `(box-set ,place ,new-form))))

used by the default arm of p-pre++, p-post++, p-pre-- and p-post--.  A
non-symbol place (an accessor form) never reaches that arm -- the arms above
it own those -- so it keeps `box-set` exactly.  Cost: one inline P-BOX-P on a
path that already calls perl-increment out of line; the hot statement-root
incdec still takes p-incf-raw and is untouched.

GUARD: Pl/t/raw-verdict-01.t rows 53-58 (plan 52 -> 58).  Every loop carries
an INDEPENDENT iteration counter as its bound -- a bound written on the
accumulated value does not work, because with the bug the sum stays 0 and the
row HANGS THE GATE instead of failing (measured both ways on a c80b1a0
worktree).  Inverse guard: row 55 fails there with "0 168 14 14" vs perl's
"14 7 14 14"; rows 53/54 (the shape) and 56-58 (PCL_OPT=none and the boxed
path) pass on both sides.

RESIDUE, not fixed here: the emitter still cannot see the verdicts, so the
compiler-layer fix (emit the raw twin for a value-consuming incdec on a raw
slot, saving the runtime type test) is still open.  It needs the verdict
threaded into Pl/ExprToCL.pm, which is plumbing this task deliberately did
not do -- the runtime fix is correct for every hole, present and future,
which the emitter fix would not be.
subject: FIXED s469bh: a value-CONSUMING ++/-- on a raw-verdict slot stored NOTHING (`box-set` on a non-box is a no-op), so `for (my $i = f(4); -- $i;)` LOOPED FOREVER on c80b1a0 -- one shared store-back decision in the four incdec macros
